protocol: 3 rounds x 3 proposals; one positive scoring winner at most per round

descriptor_candidates.name: conf_free_volume_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with the ratio of confinement volume (molecular Vol) to accessible pore volume (AV expressed per mass converted to zeolite frame), so a normalized confinement descriptor will reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below the 14-input baseline by resolving degenerate cases where pores are large but molecules compact.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: adsorbed molecules lose translational/rotational degrees of freedom roughly in proportion to how tightly the accessible pore volume constrains the molecule's own van der Waals volume. Inference (not source evidence): classical configurational entropy arguments suggest s_ads/s_gas approaches 1 as confinement weakens.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R for the network with this descriptor added (or replacing raw Vol/AV inputs' linear usage) exceeds the full-14-input baseline MAE, or if residuals show no correlation with the descriptor (|Pearson r| < 0.15 across the dataset), the hypothesis is rejected.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_anisotropy_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed primarily by the smallest pore-limiting dimension relative to the molecule's largest geometric span: entropy loss/R increases sharply when min(lsd_p, lsd_f)/SPAN approaches 1 (molecule barely fits), and saturates near a constant when the ratio is large.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: rotational freedom is lost first along the direction where pore windows barely exceed the molecular span; small-window diffusion (window-only passage) imposes the strongest orientation constraints regardless of total pore volume. This distinguishes cage-vs-window-controlled entropy regimes.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis fails if (i) adding this descriptor does not decrease MAE relative to baseline, or (ii) MAE improvement is achieved but the descriptor's effect is monotone-linear rather than saturating when regressed against entropy loss/R (a log-saturation fit not outperforming linear, indicating window-fit is not the controlling mechanism).

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_area_entropy_density
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss depends on the molecule's surface-area-to-size ratio (contact area available for adsorbent interactions per unit bulk) modulated by molecular shape eccentricity (PBF/GeDi); elongated molecules with high contact-area density lose disproportionately more rotational entropy, and log-form of this interaction term will improve MAE over the baseline.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: adsorption entropy reduction is driven by molecule-surface contact that freezes rotations and vibrations; LabuteASA normalized by molecular bulk (density*Vol) measures specific contact capacity, while PBF/GeDi encodes prolateness, which correlates with orientational pinning in channels. Inference from established adsorption thermodynamics (surface-area correlations are known); the specific nonlinear combination is proposed as new.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Rejected if MAE of entropy loss/R with this descriptor is not lower than the baseline, or if the descriptor shows |Spearman rho| < 0.1 with residuals of the baseline model, indicating it re-expresses information already captured by the 14 inputs without adding mechanism-relevant structure.

descriptor_candidates.name: pore_window_translational_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R is controlled by the ratio of the pore's two limiting window dimensions to the molecule's effective cross-sectional size (Vol^(2/3)); when this ratio approaches 1, translational freedom along the channel is maximally frozen, and adding this descriptor to the 14-input network will reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below 0.5478 by separating channel-dominated from cage-dominated adsorption cases that raw lsd_p, lsd_f and Vol cannot disambiguate linearly.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference, not source evidence): in channel-type zeolites the adsorbate's translational entropy loss is set by how the pore window cross-section (lsd_p x lsd_f product) compares with the molecule's effective cross-section, estimated as Vol^(2/3). A ratio near 1 means a tight window fit with strongly hindered translation; large ratios indicate free translation. This dimensional grouping differs from the retained volume-ratio descriptor, which captures bulk confinement rather than window-controlled translation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Rejected if MAE(entropy loss/R) with this descriptor added does not fall below 0.5478, or if the descriptor's partial dependence is non-monotone in the physically expected direction (decreasing entropy loss with increasing ratio), indicating the window-fit mechanism is not operative.

descriptor_candidates.name: rotational_pinning_aspect
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Rotational entropy loss scales with the product of molecular rotational degeneracy (encoded by the principal-moment ratio PMI3/PMI1) and the geometric tightness of fit (smallest pore dimension over molecular gyration-like diameter GeDi); elongated molecules in tight windows lose more rotational entropy than compact molecules at equal tightness, so this interaction descriptor will reduce MAE below 0.5478.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from statistical mechanics of hindered rotors, established as a known class of relations but new combination here): a near-spherical molecule (PMI3/PMI1 ~ 1) retains orientational degeneracy even in tight confinement, while a prolate molecule (large PMI3/PMI1) in a window barely wider than GeDi loses up to two rotational degrees of freedom. The multiplicative log-aspect times tightness form targets this rotor-pinning regime, distinct from translational (window ratio) and volumetric (retained) mechanisms.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Rejected if MAE does not improve below 0.5478, or if residual analysis shows the descriptor correlates with entropy loss only through its GeDi/lsd factor (|Spearman rho| of the PMI3/PMI1 factor alone with residuals < 0.1), showing the rotational-degeneracy interaction adds no mechanism-relevant information.

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_contact_compaction
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss correlates with specific surface-contact opportunity: the square root of molecular accessible surface (sqrt(LabuteASA)) per unit of zeolite accessible pore volume per mass (AV*density, source scale). High contact-area molecules hosted in low-porosity frameworks experience more molecule-wall contact constraints per degree of freedom, so this descriptor will reduce MAE below 0.5478 by capturing surface-interaction-driven vibrational/librational entropy loss that volume-based descriptors miss.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference): beyond translational/rotational freezing, adsorption entropy includes librational and vibrational softening governed by molecule-wall contact area. sqrt(LabuteASA) scales like a linear contact dimension, and dividing by framework porosity measure (AV*density) yields a contact-intensity per framework-mass measure. This targets a vibrational/librational entropy regime not addressed by the retained volumetric or window-fit descriptors. AV and density retain their source numerical scales; no unit assignment beyond that is claimed.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Rejected if MAE of entropy loss/R does not fall below 0.5478, or if the descriptor's improvement disappears when the retained conf_free_volume_ratio descriptor is simultaneously present (marginal gain < 0.002 in MAE_R), indicating it only re-expresses confinement volume information already captured.

descriptor_candidates.name: interstitial_slack_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R is governed by the slack space remaining for a molecule inside the largest pore aperture relative to the total pore-plus-molecular volume scale: when the cube of the largest free dimension dwarfs the combined volume term (free translation, low entropy loss), whereas slack near molecular scale (tight confinement, high entropy loss). Adding this descriptor to the 14-input network will reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below the round-2 benchmark 0.5478 by distinguishing open-pore weak-confinement cases from dense-framework tight confinement that raw lsd and volume inputs conflate.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference, not source evidence): translational entropy loss tracks the ratio of free-flight length scale to available volume; a cubic aperture scale over a combined framework-pore + molecular volume term measures how much of the confining space is 'window-like' versus 'cage-like'. Unlike the retained volumetric ratio (Vol vs AV) and round-2 window-product descriptor (window cross-section vs molecular cross-section), this uses the maximum aperture as a length-scale proxy cubed, targeting the regime where one large window direction dominates mobility (channels with one wide dimension).
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Rejected if MAE(entropy loss/R) with this descriptor added does not fall below 0.5478, or if the descriptor's partial dependence on maximum(lsd_p, lsd_f)**3/(Vol + AV*density) is non-monotone with |Spearman rho| < 0.1 against baseline residuals, indicating the free-flight length-scale mechanism is not operative.

descriptor_candidates.name: moment_span_compatibility
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R depends on the mismatch between the molecule's inertial shape anisotropy (PMI2/PMI1) and its geometric elongation (SPAN/GeDi), scaled by the aperture aspect ratio (lsd_f/lsd_p): molecules whose mass distribution is more anisotropic than their outer envelope (heteroatom clustering, branching) experience extra hindered-rotor entropy loss in non-circular windows, and this mismatch interaction will reduce MAE below 0.5478 by capturing internal-mass-distribution effects invisible to purely geometric inputs.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference): for a rigid rotor in an asymmetric window, rotational freezing depends on how mass is distributed relative to the envelope, not just on outer dimensions. A log-ratio of inertial to geometric anisotropy is positive when mass is concentrated off-center (e.g., branched or heteroatom-bearing adsorbates); multiplied by the window ellipticity it targets orientation-pinning in elliptical channels, a regime distinct from the retained volumetric descriptor and the rejected PMI3/PMI1 tightness product (which failed, suggesting only the anisotropy-mismatch form carries new signal).
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Rejected if MAE does not improve below 0.5478, or if shuffling the log-anisotropy-mismatch factor (replacing it with its absolute value or with 1) yields equal or better MAE (difference < 0.002), showing the mismatch mechanism adds nothing beyond window ellipticity alone.

descriptor_candidates.name: packing_density_deficit
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R combines two surface-regime factors: (i) an exponentially damped framework surface-intensity term ASA/(density*AV) capturing how much framework surface is packed per unit pore volume (high surface intensity -> more molecule-wall vibrational constraints), and (ii) a molecular compactness term Vol/LabuteASA^1.5 (compact molecules with small surface per volume lose less configurational entropy at equal confinement). Their product will reduce MAE below 0.5478 by resolving cases where equal volumetric confinement yields different entropy loss due to differing surface contact regimes.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference): the exponential damping maps surface intensity into a bounded 0-1 accessibility-like factor, avoiding the unbounded scaling that hurt the rejected surface_contact_compaction descriptor, while the Vol/ASA^1.5 factor encodes molecular compactness (a sphere maximizes Vol/ASA^1.5). The product targets the librational/vibrational entropy regime driven by framework surface contact intensity per pore volume, complementary to (not redundant with) the retained volumetric confinement ratio.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Rejected if MAE(entropy loss/R) does not fall below 0.5478, or if adding this descriptor alongside the retained conf_free_volume_ratio gives marginal MAE gain < 0.002 (indicating it re-expresses confinement volume information), or if |Pearson r| between this descriptor and the retained descriptor exceeds 0.9 in the dataset (redundancy check).
